title: Trump says he will hold off on fresh Iran attack in hope of quick deal
gist: Trump said the US will hold off a fresh attack on Iran if a deal is quickly reached to end Iran's nuclear threat and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has largely closed — a waterway carrying 20% of the world's oil and LNG before the war. Brent crude jumped 24% as an April ceasefire unravelled last month, and Israel's energy minister said Israel will strike regardless of any agreement if Iran revives its nuclear or ballistic missile programmes.

themes.theme: Hormuz closure as the inflation channel

insights.claim: Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried 20% of the world's oil and LNG before the war, pushing energy prices up and stoking broader inflation.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Quantifies the supply at risk — a fifth of seaborne oil and LNG — making Hormuz status the dominant input to global energy-driven CPI.
insights.quote: Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, a conduit for 20% of the world's oil and LNG before the war, causing energy prices to rise and stoking broader inflation.
insights.locator: Iran has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz

insights.claim: Benchmark Brent crude futures jumped 24% as an April 2026 ceasefire in the US-Iran war unravelled last month, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this year.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: A hard 24% move gives the beta of crude to ceasefire failure — and consensus positioning is still for higher prices into year-end.
insights.quote: As an April ceasefire in the war unravelled last month, benchmark Brent crude futures jumped 24%, and analysts polled by Reuters expect prices to rise further this year.

insights.claim: Trump argues that preventing Iranian nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the near term, but the economic pain is generating political pressure on him to end the war.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The pain threshold in US pump prices is the real constraint on how long Washington sustains the campaign — watch retail gasoline as the de-escalation trigger.
insights.quote: Trump has argued that his stated goal of keeping Iran from gaining nuclear weapons justifies higher fuel costs in the near term, but the economic pain has put political pressure on him to find a way to end the war.
insights.locator: Trump has argued that his stated goal

insights.claim: Iran's Houthi allies in Yemen have begun threatening the Bab el-Mandeb strait at the other end of the Red Sea from the Suez Canal, another export route for Saudi crude, adding to energy industry concerns.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The alternative route for Saudi barrels is being threatened simultaneously, removing the main mitigant analysts had assumed for a Hormuz closure.
insights.locator: Adding to the energy industry's concerns

insights.claim: Trump said Iran and unnamed Middle Eastern countries asked for time to complete a deal producing the 'Immediate, Complete and Total' reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and an end to Iran's nuclear threat, in a post following a call with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Both terms are maximalist; a deal on these terms would be a step-change for shipping and crude, but the bar for agreement is correspondingly high.
insights.quote: "Based on this request, I have agreed, for the future benefit of the WORLD and, likewise, the survival of a successful and prosperous Iran, to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL,"
insights.locator: Trump said late on Saturday on his Truth Social platform

insights.claim: Trump said at a Friday cabinet meeting that his negotiating team of Jared Kushner, special envoy Steve Witkoff and Secretary of State Marco Rubio could reach a deal with Iran.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Names the channel to monitor — movement by Witkoff or Kushner is the earliest observable signal of a genuine deal versus rhetoric.
insights.locator: At a cabinet meeting on Friday, Trump said

insights.claim: Trump and Netanyahu met in Washington on Tuesday and, per an Israeli official, explored all possible paths to curb Iran's nuclear programme including diplomacy, economic pressure and force, while Tehran denies seeking a nuclear weapon.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Force remains explicitly on the table in the same week as the announced pause, capping how much de-escalation should be priced.
insights.locator: Trump and Netanyahu met on Tuesday in Washington

insights.claim: Israeli energy minister Eli Cohen, a member of Netanyahu's security cabinet, said Israel will strike if Iran attempts to renew its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, with or without an agreement and regardless of any external commitments.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Israel has pre-committed to acting outside any US-Iran deal, meaning a signed agreement would not remove the strike risk embedded in energy prices.
insights.quote: "With or without an agreement, and regardless of any external commitments, if Iran attempts to renew its nuclear programme or advance its ballistic missile industries, we will be there. We will take action, and we will strike."

insights.claim: Israel and the United States maintain close security and intelligence coordination on everything happening in the region, according to Israeli energy minister Eli Cohen.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Reduces the odds of an unsanctioned Israeli surprise strike but also means US restraint decisions carry Israeli buy-in.
insights.locator: said there was close security and intelligence coordination

insights.claim: Iran's acting defence minister Brigadier General Majid Ebn Al-Reza said Tehran views recent US threats as 'psychological and cognitive warfare' but is taking them seriously and will boost preparedness and deterrence rather than remain passive.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Tehran is responding to the pause by building capability, not standing down — the military balance keeps worsening during diplomacy.
insights.locator: Iran’s acting defence minister, Brigadier General Majid Ebn Al-Reza

insights.claim: Attacks in the five-month US-Israel war on Iran have spread across the Gulf to the Red Sea and even to a Mediterranean facility in Egypt.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Theatre expansion to the Mediterranean means European-facing energy and shipping assets, not just Gulf ones, now carry war risk.
insights.quote: Attacks have spread across the Gulf to the Red Sea and even a Mediterranean facility in Egypt.
insights.locator: Trump's apparent de-escalation after days of threats

insights.claim: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations reported two maritime incidents off Oman on Saturday: an unknown projectile struck a tanker damaging its engine room, and another tanker master reported a large splash and nearby explosion without damage.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Confirmed hull damage off Oman during a declared pause supports higher war-risk premiums for Gulf of Oman transits regardless of diplomatic headlines.
insights.locator: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said on Saturday
